makeSendInvitation.summary: Return an invitation to send assets from an ERTP purse to an account on another chain.

registerChain.summary: Register a chain the local ChainHub does not already know, optionally with its IBC connection from the Agoric chain.

registerAsset.summary: Register a denom that may be held on a chain other than the one that issued it. Its chainName and baseName must already be registered.

makeSendInvitation.summary: Send a single asset to an address on another chain. The destination is given in offer args, not in the proposal.

published.summary: A line of progress text per step of the sendIt flow. A placeholder until Agoric/agoric-sdk#9066 gives orchestration a real progress channel.

notes: send-anywhere moves a single asset out of an ERTP purse to an account on another chain, over IBC for a Cosmos destination or over CCTP by way of Noble for USDC.
This is the guard: interface half of the Stage 0 pair. Both facets are zone.exo with M.interface, so unlike Offer Up every method here states its call kind, its parameters and its return pattern.
The creator facet is not the contract's own: it is prepareChainHubAdmin from @agoric/orchestration, which lets an operator teach the local ChainHub about a chain agoricNames does not carry yet.

The proposal uses the raw 'shape' form rather than the projected give/want form, and that is the point of it being here. The shape is M.splitRecord({ give: SingleNatAmountRecord }), which says 'exactly one give keyword, whatever it is called, holding any nat amount'. There is no keyword to project, so projecting would mean inventing one.
The destination is in offerArgs, not the proposal: { chainName, destAddr }. A client reading only the proposal would not know where the assets are going, which is worth knowing about this contract.

Every ref here names a shape exported by a package, so each carries a module and a generator can resolve it. That is the difference from Offer Up, whose refs name values that only exist once the contract has started.

terms is empty: the contract declares no meta.customTermsShape. It does read zcf.getTerms().brands.USDC, so it must be started with a USDC issuer keyword, which is a requirement the terms section cannot currently express. That is a gap worth raising before Release 6.

privateArgs is OrchestrationPowers plus marshaller, storageNode and the two optional ChainHub seeds. withOrchestration destructures marshaller out and passes the rest through, and publishAccountInfo: true means storageNode is required rather than optional here.

traces is absent: this contract is not instrumented. The multi-hop fixture in fixtures/trace-event/v0/valid/multi-hop-send-anywhere.json shows what it would emit once VowScope instruments it in Release 7, which is the intended join between the two formats.
